examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 쟁쟁한 선수들이 많이 나와요.
examples.en: Many outstanding players are entering this tournament.
The competition is so formidable that I'm nervous.
I'm nervous about presenting among such distinguished seniors.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 들은 할머니의 목소리가 아직도 귀에 쟁쟁해요.
examples.en: My grandmother's voice from when I was little still rings in my ears.
The candidates on our team were all impressive too.

examples.ko: 이 회사에는 쟁쟁한 경력의 사람들이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: People with impressive careers are gathered at this company.

explain: 실력이나 경력이 만만치 않은 사람들이 여럿 있을 때 '쟁쟁한 경쟁자들'처럼 관형형으로 많이 써요. 한 사람만 유명할 때보다 '쟁쟁한 후보들'처럼 여럿이 모인 상황에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그날 들은 박수 소리가 지금도 귀에 쟁쟁해요.
phrases.en: The applause I heard that day still rings in my ears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예전에 들은 소리가 지금도 또렷이 들리는 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sound you heard long ago still seems to echo clearly.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the modifier form, like '쟁쟁한 경쟁자들', when several people with serious skill or experience are gathered. It fits a group, such as '쟁쟁한 후보들', better than a single famous person.

examples.en: Don't give up over a trifle like that.
Why is a bag like that so expensive?

examples.ko: 저까짓 거 저도 충분히 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A little thing like that, I can do it too.
I don't mind walking through a bit of rain like that.

examples.ko: 저까짓 시험 하나 때문에 울지 말아요.
examples.en: Don't cry over one measly test like that.
Don't mind a remark like that.

explain: 눈앞이나 멀리 있는 것, 방금 말한 것을 대수롭지 않게 여기거나 얕잡아 볼 때 써요. 꼭 뒤에 '일, 거, 시험'처럼 명사가 와야 하고, 사람에게 쓰면 무례하게 들려요.
explain_en: You use it to wave away something in view or just mentioned as unimportant. A noun must follow it, such as '일' or '시험', and using it about a person sounds rude.

examples.ko: 저깟 것쯤이야 금방 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can finish a little thing like that in no time.
Don't be shaken by a rumor like that.
I can easily get over a little hill like that.
What's so important about a score like that?
Don't fight with your friend over something that petty.
Everyone makes a small mistake like that.

explain: '저까짓'의 준말이라 뜻은 같고, 말할 때 더 가볍고 빠르게 나와요. '저깟 거'처럼 뒤에 명사를 꼭 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is the shortened form of '저까짓' with the same meaning, and it sounds lighter and quicker in speech. A noun always follows it, as in '저깟 거'.

examples.en: That player is famous for his aggressive style of play.
My younger brother is the type to charge right to the front.

examples.ko: 저돌적인 영업 방식 덕분에 계약을 따냈어요.
examples.en: Thanks to his bold sales approach, he won the contract.
If you push that aggressively, the other person feels pressured.

examples.ko: 신입 사원이 저돌적인 태도로 질문을 던졌어요.
examples.en: The new employee fired off questions with a bold attitude.

examples.ko: 저돌적인 사람이 한 명 있으면 팀 분위기가 달라져요.
examples.en: With one pushy go-getter on board, the team's mood changes.

explain: '적극적이다'보다 앞뒤를 재지 않고 거침없이 밀어붙이는 느낌이 강해요. 칭찬으로 쓰면 용감하고 추진력 있다는 뜻이고, 못마땅할 때 쓰면 무모하다는 뜻이 돼요. '저돌적인 공격', '저돌적으로 달려들다'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '적극적이다' (proactive), it suggests charging ahead without hesitation. As praise it means bold and driven; when said with disapproval it means reckless. Common patterns are '저돌적인 공격' and '저돌적으로 달려들다'.

examples.en: Don't pay attention to lousy talk like that.

examples.ko: 저딴 식으로 일하면 곧 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: If you work in a sloppy way like that, problems will come soon.
What kind of song is that junk?

examples.ko: 저딴 사람 때문에 기분 상하지 마요.
examples.en: Don't let someone like that ruin your mood.
Who would wear clothes like that?

examples.ko: 저딴 영화를 왜 돈 주고 봤을까요?
examples.en: Why did I pay money to watch a movie like that?

explain: '저런'에 못마땅한 마음이 실려서 대상을 깎아내리는 말이에요. '저까짓'은 대수롭지 않다는 느낌이고, '저딴'은 마음에 안 든다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 사람 앞에서 그 사람이나 물건을 가리키면 무례해요.
explain_en: It means 'that kind of' with disapproval, so it belittles the target. '저까짓' feels like 'no big deal', while '저딴' feels more like 'I don't like it'. Pointing at someone's person or belongings with it is rude.

examples.ko: 아이가 저리도 슬프게 우는 이유가 뭘까요?
examples.en: What could be the reason the child is crying so sadly?
He works so hard, so he'll pass, right?
My friend is so happy about getting a present.
The weather is so clear, and you're staying home?
It's amazing that he walked such a long way.
Why is that person so quiet?

explain: '저렇게'와 뜻은 비슷하지만 감탄이나 안타까움, 의문이 섞인 말투예요. '왜 저리도 ~ㄹ까요?'처럼 혼잣말이나 의문문에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is close to '저렇게' (like that), but carries admiration, pity or wonder. It fits musing or questions such as '왜 저리도 ~ㄹ까요?'.

examples.en: I sat for a long time, so my toes are tingling.
My hand is tingling, so it's hard to hold a pen.
My heart aches a little when I hear that song.

examples.ko: 다리가 저릿하면 잠깐 일어나 걸어 보세요.
examples.en: If your leg tingles, stand up and walk for a moment.
My arm tingled but it was fine soon after.

examples.ko: 추운 날 밖에 있었더니 귀가 저릿하게 아파요.
examples.en: I was outside on a cold day, and my ears sting.

explain: '발이 저리다'처럼 '저리다'와 아주 비슷하게 쓰는데, '저릿하다'는 살짝 찌릿한 느낌을 말해요. 몸뿐 아니라 마음이 찡하게 아픈 느낌에도 써요.
explain_en: It is used much like '저리다', as in '발이 저리다', but describes a slight tingling sensation. Besides the body, it also expresses a pang of emotional ache.

examples.ko: 오늘 행사에는 저명인사 여러 분이 참석해요.
examples.en: Several prominent figures are attending today's event.
He is regarded as a prominent figure in the industry.
It was a talk by a notable person, so the seats filled fast.
I took a photo with some distinguished people.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 저명인사가 된 졸업생이 많아요.
examples.en: This school has many graduates who became prominent figures.

examples.ko: 저명인사라고 해서 모두 친절한 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Not every prominent person is kind.

explain: 학계, 정치, 문화처럼 한 분야에서 이름이 널리 알려진 사람을 점잖게 부르는 말이에요. 연예인에게는 보통 '유명인'이나 '연예인'이라고 하고, '저명인사'는 격식 있는 자리나 기사에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is a polished way to call someone widely known in a field such as academia, politics or culture. For entertainers people usually say '유명인' or '연예인'; '저명인사' suits formal occasions and articles.

examples.en: As dusk came, the lights in the street came on.
I like walking along the beach at dusk.
At dusk the sky turns red.
At dusk, my grandmother is sweeping the yard.
A winter dusk gets dark quickly.
We only reached the foot of the mountain at dusk.

explain: '해 질 녘'과 거의 같은 말이에요. '저녁'보다 해가 지는 바로 그 무렵을 가리키고, 말보다는 글이나 노랫말에서 잘 어울려요. 반대로 해가 뜰 무렵은 '동틀 녘'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is nearly the same as '해 질 녘'. Rather than the whole evening, it points to the moment the sun is setting, and suits writing and lyrics more than casual speech. The opposite, around sunrise, is '동틀 녘'.

examples.en: Please slice the onion thinly.
I slice ginger and put it in the tea.
Mom sliced the meat thin and grilled it for me.
My heart is wrenched by the child's crying.
Please mince the garlic instead of slicing it.

examples.ko: 그 이야기를 들으니 마음이 저미는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: Hearing that story felt like my heart was being cut.

explain: '썰다'보다 얇고 납작하게 도려내는 느낌이라 고기, 생강, 마늘 같은 재료에 써요. 마음에는 '가슴이 저미다', '가슴 저미는'처럼 쓰는데, 칼로 에는 듯 아프다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: My heart aches reading my grandmother's letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬픔이나 안타까움 때문에 가슴이 에는 듯 아플 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sadness or pity makes your chest ache as if it were being cut.

explain_en: Compared with '썰다' (to cut), it means cutting thin, flat slices, used for meat, ginger or garlic. For emotions, '가슴이 저미다' or '가슴 저미는' says the heart feels as if cut by a knife.

examples.en: I hear heavy footsteps in the hallway.
He walked with heavy steps toward the door.
I came home crunching through the snowy path.

examples.ko: 밤길에 뒤에서 저벅저벅 소리가 나서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled by footsteps behind me on the night road.
My father walked in with firm steps.

examples.ko: 조용한 길에 저벅저벅 걷는 소리만 울렸어요.
examples.en: Only the sound of tramping steps echoed on the quiet road.

explain: 무겁고 또렷하게 걷는 발소리나 모양을 흉내 낸 말이에요. 힘없이 걷는 '터벅터벅'과 달리 저벅저벅은 당당하고 묵직한 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound or manner of walking with heavy, clear steps. Unlike '터벅터벅', which sounds weary, '저벅저벅' feels firm and weighty.

examples.ko: 두 회사 중 어디로 갈지 저울질해요.
examples.en: I'm weighing which of the two companies to go to.
I keep weighing whether to change jobs or not.

examples.ko: 가격과 품질을 저울질한 끝에 이걸 샀어요.
examples.en: After weighing price against quality, I bought this one.

examples.ko: 어느 쪽이 더 이익인지 저울질하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't calculate which side benefits you more.

examples.ko: 친구는 두 사람 사이에서 저울질하다가 둘 다 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: My friend kept weighing two people and lost both.

examples.ko: 여행 날짜를 저울질해 보고 다시 연락할게요.
examples.en: I'll weigh the travel dates and get back to you.

explain: 그냥 '고민하다'가 아니라 어느 쪽이 더 이득인지 비교해 보는 느낌이에요. 사람 사이에서 이쪽저쪽을 재면 계산적이라는 부정적인 뉘앙스가 생겨요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '고민하다' (to worry over), it means comparing options to see which gains more. When used between people, it hints at being calculating, which sounds negative.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 상사 앞에서 늘 저자세예요.
examples.en: He is always submissive in front of his boss.
If you act too meekly in a negotiation, you lose out.
Why do you act so meekly only toward that person?
I apologized to the customer in a very humble manner.
He started out humble, then suddenly changed his attitude.
Being humble doesn't mean being weak.

explain: 예의 바른 것과 달리 상대에게 눌려 굽실거리는 느낌이 있어서 좋은 뜻만은 아니에요. '저자세로 나가다/나오다', '저자세를 취하다'로 자주 쓰고, 반대말은 '고자세'예요.
explain_en: Unlike simply being polite, it suggests cowering before the other side, so it isn't purely positive. Common patterns are '저자세로 나가다/나오다' and '저자세를 취하다'; the opposite is '고자세'.

examples.en: He harbors hostility toward his rival.
The child's eyes were full of hostility.

examples.ko: 오해 때문에 서로 적개심을 갖게 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of a misunderstanding, they came to feel hostile toward each other.
If you show hostility, conversation becomes difficult.
Hostility destroyed the teamwork.
Where did that kind of hostility come from?

explain: '적대감'과 비슷하지만 적개심은 상대와 싸우려는 마음이 더 강하게 느껴져요. '적개심을 품다', '적개심을 드러내다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '적대감', but '적개심' feels more like a will to fight the other side. Typical collocations are '적개심을 품다' and '적개심을 드러내다'.

examples.en: I felt hostility from the moment we first met.
His way of speaking carried hostility.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에 적대감이 점점 커지고 있어요.
examples.en: Hostility between the two countries is growing.

examples.ko: 적대감을 풀려면 먼저 대화를 해야 해요.
examples.en: To dissolve the hostility, you have to talk first.

examples.ko: 저를 적대감 어린 눈으로 보지 마세요.
examples.en: Please don't look at me with hostile eyes.
Long-standing hostility doesn't vanish overnight.

explain: 상대를 적처럼 대하는 감정이라서 사람뿐 아니라 집단이나 나라 사이에도 써요. '적대감을 느끼다/드러내다/풀다'처럼 쓰고, '적대감 어린 눈빛'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of treating someone as an enemy, so it applies to people as well as groups and countries. It goes with verbs like '느끼다', '드러내다' and '풀다', and also appears in '적대감 어린 눈빛'.
